{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.00) to counteract overestimation bias.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) when mean reversion is likely, especially if recent prices are high.",
    "Increase forecast lag by 1–2 days if sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.00) to avoid overshoot after spikes.",
    "Apply upward correction if true outcome is consistently below forecast in early days (e.g., 1–3 days) to reflect mean reversion.",
    "When sentiment turns positive after a low, increase forecast slope to capture momentum, but cap at 10% above recent high.",
    "If forecast consistently overestimates true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, apply a 5–10% downward bias correction.",
    "For sentiment = 0.25, apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to prevent overreaction to minor bullish signals."
  ]
}
